prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–3, the depth map places a stainless-steel stove table and vertical stall pillar immediately in front of the camera wearer at ~0.3–1.0 m (bright white/light grey), with the wearer's raised right arm in frames 2–3 reaching ~0.3–0.5 m to grasp the pillar on the right while two standing men on the sidewalk beyond the counter appear as mid-grey silhouettes at ~2.0–2.5 m (about 0.3–0.5 m apart from each other) against a pitch-black outdoor street (>5 m). Across frames 4–5, the camera wearer turns sharply rightward and downward into the kitchen interior, where the stove counter, a frying wok, small metal bowls, and a cook standing on the left holding a bowl and ladle are all within ~0.5–1.5 m (within arm's reach of both the wearer and the cook), and the wearer's left hand enters the bottom-left foreground at ~0.3 m in frame 5. The depth map makes the metric separation between the foreground counter/pillar, the middle-ground people, and the background shelves or street much clearer than RGB alone, and cleanly resolves the 3D geometry of the recessed gas burner and cooking vessels. However, it provides no facial orientation details to tell whether the men look at the camera, clips to saturated white on the closest pillar and arm in frames 1–3, and flattens everything beyond the stall opening into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: In frames 1–3, the segmentation map isolates the two standing men outside the stall (~2.0–2.5 m away, side by side with the left man's lower legs occluded by the unlabelled foreground stove counter) and tiny distant cars (~10–20 m behind them), while capturing the camera wearer's raised right arm in the right foreground (~0.3–0.5 m) in frames 2–3. In frames 4–5, as the camera turns right into the kitchen, it segments the nearby cook on the left (~0.8–1.2 m away, head cropped at the top edge), the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom-left of frame 5 (~0.3 m), and several vessels within arm's reach (~0.5–1.5 m) including the wok, small metal pots, the handheld bowl and ladle (`spoon`), and distant background bowls (~2.5–3.0 m). The map helps separate overlapping person instances, utensil boundaries (`spoon` inside `bowl`), and tiny distant vehicles that blend into the bright street in RGB alone. However, it is highly unreliable for class labels and completeness: it completely misses the stove counter in frames 1–3, mislabels the wearer's right arm in frame 3 as `cow`, fragments the stove and kitchen backdrop into `oven`, `chair`, and `dining table`, and gives no direct cue of metric distance or gaze direction.
descriptions.pose: In frames 1–3, the pose map tracks the upper-body skeletons and facial keypoints of the two men standing side by side ~2.0–2.5 m in front of the camera wearer, showing their shoulders squared toward the stall and face keypoints oriented toward the wearer (except in frame 3 where the left man's head turns slightly to his left), with the right man's right elbow bent on his hip and single isolated ankle/knee dots below where the counter occludes their legs. In frame 3 it adds the left man's skeleton (missed in frames 1–2), and in frame 4—after the camera turns right—it captures the nearby cook's torso (~1.0 m away, tilted forward with face keypoints near the upper-left edge) and both magenta hand skeletons holding the bowl and ladle at ~0.8 m. By frame 5, as the camera pitches further down and the cook's head leaves the top of the frame, the cook's body skeleton fails to detect, leaving only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand reaching in at the bottom-left (~0.3 m). While pose skeletons clearly reveal torso orientation, head gaze direction, and two-handed gripping in frame 4 that are subtler in depth or segmentation, the map omits all scene objects and background layout, misses the left bystander in frames 1–2 and the cook's body in frame 5 due to cropping/occlusion, and fails to detect the wearer's raised right arm in frames 2–3.
